conflicts.fact: Where students observed sukuma wiki leaf cells under the microscope
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 says students revisit their own Lesson 3 microscope drawings of sukuma wiki leaf cells, but Lesson 3 covers animal-cell organelles using electron micrographs with no sukuma wiki microscopy. Lesson 1 only shows a projected image of the leaf cell, and Lesson 2 uses onion and cheek cells.

conflicts.fact: Whether the unexplained absence of green colour in onion cells is resolved in Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the question of why the onion cell lacks green colour will be explained in Lesson 4 (chloroplasts and where in a plant they are found). Lesson 4 only explains chloroplasts in sukuma wiki leaf cells and never addresses why onion epidermis has no green colour.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson students observed human cheek cells and drew them
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says students observed/drew the human cheek cell in Lesson 3, but cheek cells were prepared in the Lesson 2 microscopy practical; Lesson 3 covers animal cell organelles via electron micrographs.

conflicts.fact: Structure of the cumulative cell model from Lesson 4
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 builds two separate 2D labelled diagrams (a generalised plant cell and a generalised animal cell). Lesson 5 says the Lesson 4 model is a three-column comparison chart (Generic Eukaryotic | Animal Specialised | Plant Specialised), and its Explained section lists a different four-column set.

conflicts.fact: When the cumulative cell model began and its lesson numbering
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the cumulative model was begun in Lesson 2 and revised in Lessons 3, 4 and 5. Lesson 4 says Version 1 of the cumulative diagrams was produced in Lesson 4 and will be developed across Lessons 5–8, while Lesson 2 refers to refining it until the 3D model in Lesson 7.

conflicts.fact: Organelles in animal cells: vacuoles and centrioles
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 requires the animal cell diagram to include small vacuoles. Lesson 3 lists 10 animal organelles, including centrioles. Lessons 7 and 8 say animal cells may contain centrioles, while Lesson 8 lists them as 'unique to or more common in animal cells', and Lesson 4 omits centrioles.
Lesson 5 and Lesson 8 say four universal features: cell membrane, cytoplasm, DNA and ribosomes. Lesson 7 and Lesson 8's Explained section list only membrane, cytoplasm and genetic material (three).

conflicts.fact: White blood cell nucleus description and nucleus in anchoring phenomenon
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 and 3 describe white blood cells as having a large visible nucleus; Lesson 8 says a large lobed nucleus and many lysosomes, while Lesson 4 says both blood cell types are compared against leaf cells and that shared nucleus applies to both cell types 'in most cases', implying blood cells have nuclei despite RBCs lacking one.
